summary: The corpus separates active inflation/blowing from Detransitive swelling, while both are integrated in stem I. Finite actor suffixes in nfəḥle/nfəḥla contrast with nfiḥ/nfiḥo change or resultant-state contexts.

The technical bellows procedure repeats ordinary blowing and does not justify a craft-specific sense. New Imperativ and Infinitiv boxes and explicit Infectum-wa allocation have priority over repetitive captures of blowing.
nafoḥo blower is an occupational form retained under the entry Part act. convention. Nafóḥowayno has a past copula and does not establish finite Infectum-wa by itself; nofaḥwa/nəfḥiwa do.

Nomen Actionis nəfuḥo air current must not be relabelled Infinitiv merely to normalize boxes. Infinitiv nfoḥo denotes the blowing activity; their relationship and Detransitive filing need editorial review.

The allowed npḥ lookup confirms a parallel p-spelled entry with separate numbering and nostril-blowing examples. The f-spelled occurrences remain under nfḥ; no cross-entry renumbering or silent merger is made.
Repeated nfiḥo at 69/299 intensifies swelling, while g- and -wa blowing contexts differ in tense/aspect and narrative environment; do not infer a new meaning from either.
Confirm the relation of nfḥ and npḥ spelling variants before merging entries; npḥ.2 anschwellen lassen is numbered differently from nfḥ.2 anschwellen.
Does appe in MAC Mother Mary saves Sultan’s son/26 and /33 denote the target creatures or a location? No precise government gloss is added from it.
Confirm whether nfoḥo and nəfuḥo constitute distinct nominal formations or edition/dialect variants; preserve their existing labels until resolved.
Confirm finite nfiḥo versus adjectival state interpretation in PrS 22/4; following ḥzele permits a resultant-state reading, while the inherited Detransitive Preterit filing supports the retained box.
Reconcile PrS page/line and supplied text/verse references; no alternative numbering is silently substituted.

Blowing can target a fire, an instrument, a person or a magical figure. Magical transformation is carried by following predicates, not a new meaning of blowing; flute playing is an ordinary activity context.
